page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9ae.48xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. It provides 192 dedicated vCPUs derived from AMD EPYC 9T95 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz. Accompanying this processing capacity is 1536.0 GB of system memory, establishing a consistent memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server does not include GPU accelerators, directing its full hardware footprint toward non-accelerated CPU and memory computation.

The instance integrates a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps, which facilitates rapid communication across distributed architectures and remote data stores. Local disk storage is not bundled with this configuration, meaning all persistent storage must be provisioned through network-attached block devices. While the absence of local NVMe storage removes low-latency ephemeral disk operations, the 100 Gbps networking capacity offsets external storage access bottlenecks and ensures efficient transit for massive datasets.

By packing 192 dedicated cores and 1.5 TB of memory into a single virtualized envelope, ecs.r9ae.48xlarge offers high resource consolidation. This design reduces host-to-host network fragmentation for workloads that require large shared-memory pools. The hardware profile suits enterprise in-memory databases, real-time big data processing pipelines, large-scale extract-transform-load tasks, and memory-bound analytics engines.

It delivers 1536.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The platform contains no integrated GPU accelerators and features zero local storage, relying on external network-attached storage infrastructure. Network connectivity is supported by a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth configuration, enabling rapid multi-node synchronization and remote storage traffic. The substantial memory footprint and high core count make ecs.r9ae.48xlarge appropriate for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory database engines, large cache layers, distributed data science workflows, and complex enterprise resource planning deployments.
